ca_corral_and_double_dome.blurb: A small crag at roughly 7,900 feet in the Benton area of the Eastern Sierra, set well apart from the neighbouring crags. The formations are low, mostly around 30 feet, and the climbing is short bolted lines packed close together, plus a single trad route. Grades run from 5.7 up into the 5.10s, with the bulk between 5.8 and 5.10. The wall faces west, so it takes afternoon sun and offers little shade. The base is flat and roomy, which suits groups setting up several top ropes.

ca_crypt_the_2.blurb: The Crypt is an 80-foot pile of rock in the Planet X area of central Joshua Tree, sitting between The Love Nest and King Dome. It was developed more recently than most of its neighbours and holds eight trad routes, mostly face climbing. Two are easy lines, one is 5.7, four fall between 5.8 and 5.9, and a single route reaches the 5.11 range. That spread makes it a reasonable stop for a party climbing near the middle of the grade range.

ca_cuckoo_s_nest_the.blurb: The Cuckoo's Nest is a small climbing area at about 4,400 feet in the Echo Rock area of central Joshua Tree. It has eight routes, split evenly between trad and sport, with grades from 5.6 to the 5.10s. Most of the lines sit at 5.9 and 5.10. Getting in means hiking up and over a ridge from the first pullout past Echo Cove, then either rappelling into the canyon or following a third-class notch down.

ca_earthday_dome.blurb: Earthday Dome is a slabby dome in the Alabama Hills near Lone Pine, lying north of Whitney Cave and east of the Candy Store area at about 4,600 feet. It has eight routes, four sport and four trad, running from 5.6 to 5.9, with most at 5.7 and 5.8. The dome faces southwest and takes plenty of sun, so shade is scarce and water is worth carrying. Slab technique matters more here than strength, and some of the lines are runout.
